title: BTL1 — Partie 1: Fondamentaux, Phishing, début CTI
src: Tes notes BTL1 (Security Blue Team), questions rédigées par Claude
summary: Révision interactive tirée de tes notes: bases réseau (OSI, TCP, ports, adresses privées, commandes), analyse de phishing (artefacts, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, blocage proxy) et début de la Threat Intelligence. Les autres domaines suivront dans l'ordre du cours: Threat Intelligence, Digital Forensics, SIEM, Incident Response.
points: OSI: 1 Physical, 2 Data Link, 3 Network, 4 Transport, 5 Session, 6 Presentation, 7 Application
SPF = serveurs autorisés (TXT), DKIM = signature cryptographique, DMARC = politique + rapports
Artefacts phishing: expéditeur, Reply-To, objet, date, pièce jointe + hash SHA256, URL (défangée), IP du serveur
Blocage: URL (précis) vs domaine (large) vs DNS blackholing
Pyramid of Pain: hash et IP faciles à changer pour l'attaquant

mcq.q: Which private IPv4 range contains 16,777,216 addresses?
mcq.why: 10.0.0.0/8 = 16,777,216 addresses (Class A private).

mcq.q: Which private range holds 1,048,576 addresses?
Which private range holds 65,536 addresses?
mcq.why: 192.168.0.0/16 = 65,536 addresses, the typical home range.

mcq.q: What is the range of the well-known ports?
mcq.why: Well-known 0–1023 (FTP, SSH, DNS…); registered 1024–49151; private/ephemeral 49152–65535.

mcq.q: What are the ports 49152 – 65535 used for?
o: Ephemeral source ports chosen by the client in a client-server exchange
mcq.why: These private ports are used as the client's source port.

mcq.q: How is a MAC address written?
o: Eight groups of four hexadecimal digits
mcq.why: A MAC address is manufactured into every network card, but it can be changed (spoofed) by an attacker.

mcq.q: What are the three steps of the TCP three-way handshake?
mcq.why: Client sends SYN (random sequence number), server replies SYN-ACK (ack = client SYN + 1), client sends ACK (ack = server SYN + 1).

mcq.q: In the handshake, what does the server's SYN-ACK acknowledge?
mcq.why: ack = SYNcl + 1.

mcq.q: Which protocol is connectionless?
mcq.why: UDP has no handshake; TCP ensures reliable delivery.

mcq.q: What is ICMP used for?
o: Error reporting and diagnostics such as ping and traceroute
mcq.why: ICMP = Internet Control Message Protocol.

mcq.q: Which type of IP allocation is DHCP?
mcq.why: Static ≠ DHCP: static addresses are set by hand, DHCP assigns them dynamically.

mcq.q: Who developed the OSI model and when?
mcq.why: OSI = Open Systems Interconnection Model, developed by ISO in 1984.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer deals with the physical operation (cables, optical fibre)?
mcq.why: Ethernet cables and optical fibre are Layer 1.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer encapsulates data and separates it into frames?
mcq.why: The Data Link layer handles framing and MAC addressing.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for finding the shortest path (routing)?
mcq.why: Routers work at Layer 3 with IP addresses.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer assembles and fragments packets and uses ports?
mcq.why: TCP and UDP operate at the Transport layer.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer handles the opening, closing and resetting of sessions?
mcq.why: Session layer = managing sessions.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer performs encryption/decryption and presents data in the correct form?
mcq.why: Presentation = translator between the machine and the user.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer is the one the user directly interacts with (e-mail apps, web browsers, file transfer)?
mcq.why: HTTP and SMTP are application-layer protocols.

mcq.q: Which command shows the IP addresses of a Linux device?
mcq.why: ip a = addresses; ip r list = routing table.

mcq.q: Which command displays the routing table on Linux?
o: ip link set dev eth0 up
mcq.why: ip r list shows the current routing table.

mcq.q: What does 'ip link set dev [Device] up|down' do?
o: Enables or disables a network interface
mcq.why: It sets the interface up (enabled) or down (disabled).

mcq.q: Which tool monitors the TCP and UDP connections on a host?
mcq.why: netstat lists active connections and listening ports.

mcq.q: Which tool shows the path that packets take between two systems?
mcq.why: Used to troubleshoot issues between two systems.

mcq.q: Which tool queries a DNS server for information about a domain (for example the mail server of a domain)?
mcq.why: nslookup finds an IP address from a URL or the mail server a domain routes e-mail through.

mcq.q: In the AAA concept, what does Accountability mean?
o: Defining what the user is permitted to do
mcq.why: Authentication = verify identity; Authorization = what the user may do; Accountability = what happened and when.

mcq.q: What does DLP stand for?
mcq.why: DLP prevents sensitive data from leaving the organization.

mcq.q: In a CEO-fraud / BEC attack, what does the attacker usually do?
o: Poses as an executive and asks the finance team for an urgent transfer to an attacker-controlled account
Encrypts files and demands a ransom
Floods the mail server with traffic
mcq.why: Time pressure and authority are the key tricks.

mcq.q: What is the Reply-To address?
o: The address that receives replies to the original e-mail, which may differ from the sending address
The address of the mail server
The address of the recipient's gateway
The address used in the SPF record
mcq.why: An attacker may set Reply-To to an attacker-controlled account.

mcq.q: Why should the sent date and time of a phishing e-mail be recorded?
o: To search a period around it and find other related e-mails
To compute the hash of the e-mail
To prove the e-mail is encrypted
mcq.why: Searching on either side of the time may reveal other messages.

mcq.q: Why is the attachment name a useful artifact?
o: It can be blocked in the EDR as an indicator of compromise (name + extension)
It proves the attachment is safe
It replaces the need for a hash
mcq.why: Include the file name and file extension.

mcq.q: Why are MD5 and SHA1 no longer recommended for file hashing?
mcq.why: Prefer SHA256 for reputation checks, though generating all of them is useful.

mcq.q: Which service by Cisco lets you search a SHA256 against a reputation database?
mcq.why: VirusTotal is another reputation tool.

mcq.q: How can you find which mailboxes received the same phishing e-mail?
o: Search the email gateway for the sending address (and subject)
mcq.why: Then inform them not to interact with it.

mcq.q: Which tool provides a hostname from the sending server's IP address?
mcq.why: It helps identify whether the sending address was spoofed.

mcq.q: How should a URL from a phishing e-mail be collected?
o: Copied properly (Copy Link Destination), not typed by hand
mcq.why: Typing by hand risks mistakes that ruin the analysis.

mcq.q: If an online reputation tool does not flag a site, what should the analyst assume?
o: Nothing: treat suspicious sites as malicious until proven safe
mcq.why: 'Not malicious' ≠ 'safe'.

mcq.q: What is URLhaus (abuse.ch)?
o: A database of malicious URLs reported by researchers, with threat feeds
mcq.why: It can be used to generate blacklists of malicious URLs.

mcq.q: What is PhishTank?
o: A service where users submit phishing artifacts that are verified by the community
mcq.why: It works like URLhaus.

mcq.q: What does the 'defanged' form hxxp://domain[.]com mean?
o: The link is modified so it cannot be clicked accidentally
mcq.why: Defang before sharing a malicious URL.

mcq.q: What is the difference between a URL block and a domain block on a web proxy?
o: A URL block is very specific; a domain block stops everything on the domain
A URL block is permanent; a domain block is temporary
A URL block is for IPs; a domain block for e-mails
mcq.why: A URL block is ineffective when the attacker changes the URL on the same domain.

mcq.q: When is a domain block appropriate?
o: When the domain is malicious or compromised and employees have no business need for it
Only when the domain is Google
When the e-mail has an attachment
mcq.why: Decide whether employees would ever need the domain.

mcq.q: What is DNS blackholing?
o: Redirecting requests for a malicious domain to another site so users never reach it
mcq.why: A protective measure complementary to firewalls and proxies.

mcq.q: In the Pyramid of Pain, how do IP addresses rank for the attacker?
o: Among the easiest indicators to change (second easiest after hashes)
mcq.why: The higher in the pyramid, the more it hurts the attacker.

mcq.q: What is an SPF record?
o: A DNS TXT record listing the servers allowed to send mail for a domain, with an enforcement rule
A signature added to each e-mail
A rule on the mail gateway
mcq.why: Prevents forging of the sender address.

mcq.q: In an SPF record, what does '-all' mean?
o: Hard fail: mail from unlisted servers should be rejected
mcq.why: ~all would be a soft fail.

mcq.q: What does DKIM do?
o: Cryptographically verifies the e-mail came from a trusted server and was not altered in transit
Encrypts the e-mail body for the recipient
mcq.why: The server signs an encrypted hash of the e-mail contents.

mcq.q: What does a DMARC record define?
o: What to do when SPF/DKIM fail (e.g. quarantine) and where to send aggregate reports
The key used to sign e-mails
mcq.why: The notes show quarantine on failure plus aggregate reports sent to a mailbox.

mcq.q: Which spam filter sits behind an on-premises firewall and is typical of larger organizations?
mcq.why: Hosted filters live in the cloud and update more quickly.

mcq.q: What is the major drawback of desktop spam filters?
o: They may be freeware, and you may not know what the application installs
They only work in the cloud
mcq.why: Typically used in SOHO scenarios.

mcq.q: Why are Bayesian filters considered intelligent?
o: They learn from the user's spam markings and block similar messages
mcq.why: They use machine-learning concepts.

mcq.q: Which of these is an open-source phishing simulation tool?
mcq.why: The others are commercial simulators.

mcq.q: Which character trick is used in homograph attacks?
mcq.why: Browsers treat them as different characters while they look the same.

mcq.q: Why is a phishing e-mail's subject line a valuable artifact?
o: Attackers rarely change it, so it helps find every copy of the campaign
mcq.why: Several sending addresses may share the same subject line.

mcq.q: What is threat intelligence?
o: Information used to understand threats currently or potentially targeting the organization
A list of all firewall rules
mcq.why: It is about turning raw data into intelligence that can be used.

mcq.q: What does ELINT refer to?
o: Electronic intelligence collected from systems not used directly for communications (radars, guidance)
mcq.why: COMINT = communications intelligence (messages and voice), often synonymous with SIGINT.

mcq.q: What is a CVE?
o: A unique identifier for a publicly reported vulnerability
mcq.why: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures.

mcq.q: What does CVSS provide?
o: A severity score for vulnerabilities (e.g. Base Score 8.8 HIGH)
mcq.why: A generic guideline: real risk depends on products, versions and controls.

mcq.q: What is Tenable's VPR?
o: A score combining vulnerability data with threat intelligence to prioritize what is likely to be exploited
mcq.why: The VPR rises if a vulnerability is seen exploited in the wild.

mcq.q: In FireEye/Mandiant naming, what does the prefix FIN stand for?
mcq.why: UNC = unclassified group under analysis.

mcq.q: What is an ISAC?
o: An Information Sharing and Analysis Center: organizations in the same industry sharing intelligence
mcq.why: They share actionable and strategic intelligence to improve defenses.

mcq.q: Which weakness lets an attacker run a malicious SQL query through a web form?
mcq.why: Special characters such as / - = ` ' should not be accepted unfiltered.
